sections.content: The content is interesting if you are interested in China's Economy Development from a con-China's perspective.
sections.teaching: Professor is generally good. He is willing to teach in Office Hour, so can go for it and ask questions more often. It can help you get Good Grade.
sections.grading: Fine. I got A Range. However, I would not say it is very easy to get A Range. It needs you to dedicate certain amount of time and energy. Better not, if you just want an easy course to fulfil your credit requirement.
sections.workload: Heavy. Every week a few readings. The exams are not easy, Have Open Essay Questions. And, you need to write quite some, if you want a Good Grade.

sections.content: 讲述有关中国近现代的经济转型与发展的内容。包括但不限于讨论中国近代为何未能工业化，中国的现代农业经济制度，中国共产党对中国经济的领导作用，中国的金融体系等内容。作为文院专业课内容专业化程度较高。
sections.teaching: 教授英语很标准，基本没有英语因为口音听不懂的情况。教学内容很细致，在其中会举具体例子来解释讲的内容。ppt内容基本上涵盖了课上所讲的所有重点，考试范围大部分都在ppt上。唯一的缺点可能就是语调比较平，有时候容易让人走神。
sections.grading: 给分非常好。包括每节课后的作业，小组展示，期中考试以及期末考试。其中作业和小组展示只要按要求做完就是满分。一共有十次作业，提交八次即可。期中和期末考试有一定难度，包含选择，填空和essay。但给分很宽松，比如填空填一个与正确答案的数字近似的数字也可拿分。
sections.workload: workload量并不大，最主要的就是每周上课之后的assignment。除此之外认真按PPT上内容复习准备考试即可。

sections.content:

1. Why Care about the Chinese Economy?
2. The Problem of Causality in the Social Sciences
3. Economic History
3.1 The broad historical strokes
3.2 Why did China not industrialize earlier?
4. Reform Period Overview
5. Economic Geography
6. Central Planning and Economic Transition
6.1 The theory of centrally planned economies [6.2 The theory of market economies]
6.3 The fatal conceit: the errors of socialism
6.4 Planning in China
6.5 Transition in China
7. Economic Development
7.1 Pre-reform period economic development strategies
7.2 Reform period economic development strategies
incl. Specifically: Industrial Policy
7.2.1 Economic development: industry
7.2.2 Economic development: agriculture
7.2.3 Economic development: financial system
7.2.4 Economic development: fiscal system
7.2.5 Energy 7.2.6 Environment 7.2.7 Digital economy
7.3 Regional economic development: China’s Western region
8. Economic Decision Making
9. Governance and Ownership
10. China and the World
11. Labor, Demographics, and Education

But mostly according to the assigned reading two days before posted on Canvas. May not really strictly refer to the syllabus.
sections.teaching:
Professor has extensive knowledge about this field. He has his own insight to criticise material and issues. He will teach you the knowledge of not just the textbook but also the most updated Chinese economic issues (e.g., recent GDP, LGFVs, technological innovation, and new productive forces). Some of them can be quite sensitive, but you can get a multi-view regard to China's economy and related fields.

He doesn't like to regulate students's thoughts and always encourages students to express their own views, but he does not require all people to speak in class. He always uses questionnaires to collect students's opinions to set the syllabus. You are quite free to choose a term paper or exam.
sections.grading:
Official grading:
1) 16% One 1-page (maximum 500 word) interpretative précis of a reading in the syllabus with a maximum 10-minute presentation to the class, followed by a brief open discussion in class. — Graded pass/fail. — Place the précis in ‘Discussions’ on CANVAS at least 24 hours before the class meets. — Starts Week 5. — Team work of up to three students is welcome. — Also see details re précis towards the end of the syllabus.
2) 16% Assignments, typically assigned weekly on Thursday and due the following Tuesday (8* 2%). — Expect a 30-90 minute effort. — Graded pass/fail. — We should have 10 assignments in total (maximally 8 assignments count). — We may also have “10-minute” mini assignments, typically assigned Tuesday, due Thursday, not submitted, not graded.
3) 34% Midterm exam 1, in class, closed book
4) 34% Midterm exam 2, in class, closed book
sections.workload: If you take the reading seriously, then you will be quite confused. Instead, just focus on his PPT (he provides a summary of reading) and assignment (he took a question from the assignment  in the final exam, nearly 90% of the of the question from the lesson discussion, his view, assignment, and summary of reading instead of the lesson PPTs), and you can achieve a good grade.

sections.content:
**no official textbook**, however, as an idiot of Economics and Chinese political structure, go to read Barry Naughton's book: The Chinese Economy: Transitions of Growth.

This is a mix course of Economics and Politics. Economic Theory is important, esp. Macro-, Updated knowledge in Chinese political structure is also important.

Some readings that I recommend you to read even you are not in the class.
1) Victor Shih: Financial instability in China
2) Elvin Mark: Quantitative Growth, Qualitative Standstill
3) Qian Yingyi: How reform worked in China
4) Mao Zedong: On 10 major relationships (an interesting article in testing your logic)
5) Vivienne Shue: From Heshang to Falungong
6) Michael Hout: A Chinese Approach to Management
7) Perry Link: The Anaconda in the Chandelier: Chinese Censorship Today

After you read this, you will gain better knowledge in knowing what's going on in China. Nowadays, when you are seeking for jobs, these knowledge are helpful.

Personally, I like the topic on Sociology of Scholars doing China Studies most. This is something you won't see in normal Economics Class, but only Holz's class
sections.teaching:
Super easy-going professor.
He won't take attendance.
He won't urge you to do homework.
He won't force people doing something they don't like.
sections.grading:
the marking scheme of mid-term is lenient.

Critique: P/F only (in other words, if you have properly done it, you will gain 20 points)

Mid-term: only 1/3 of students take this:
full mark: 70, mean: 67.1, highest: 70, lowest: 60

final:
full mark: 88, mean: 65.9, highest: 83, lowest: 46

total score (100%):
mean: 81.5 (except the one who score 0), highest: 97

Absolutely good grade. Only Prof. Holz can make this. Take this course, when Prof. Holz runs.
sections.workload:
Optional combination of workload:
All required: One critique (20%) + Final exam (80%, cumulative)

Optional:
Combo 1: Critique (20%) + midterm exam (30%) + final exam (50%)
Combo 2: Critique (20%) + term paper (15%) + midterm exam (30%) + final exam (35%)
You can choose any combo as you like. You can just complete the work as required. However, you cannot shift to any other combo after you have picked one.

sections.content: It is not based on textbook. Pr selects the reading materials that fits more to the current state of china's poli econ market. You would have to have econ and social science background for this course.
sections.teaching: You have to read the readings before the lecture!!! the selected readings are bit tough, but the professor explains at the lecture very well. There is no ppt slide, it requires both discussion and notetaking.
sections.grading: Midterm and Final Exams are both in essay format.
sections.workload: There is required reading for each lecture, and it is very very important!!   It requires constant hardworking in order to catch up in the course. But worth it!
